title: Network configuration
subtitle: Live interfaces, routes, persistent files, and NSS

cards.meaning: NIC name Linux uses to talk TCP/IP
cards.notes: Inspect/change live with ifconfig or ip; persist in distro config files.

cards.front: ifconfig / ip vs ifcfg-* / interfaces vs nsswitch.conf
cards.meaning: now vs after reboot vs where to look up names
cards.notes: Live tools change runtime; distro files survive reboot; NSS picks files/DNS/LDAP order.

cards.meaning: Configure/control TCP/IP interfaces (set IP/netmask, enable/disable)
cards.notes: Shows interfaces that are currently up. Legacy net-tools; RHEL 7+ prefers ip.

cards.meaning: List all interfaces, including those that are down
cards.notes: -a = even the sleeping NICs.

cards.meaning: Show one named interface
Activate (bring up) the interface
cards.notes: down deactivates. Logical on/off — not unplugging the cable.

cards.meaning: Legacy net-tools; new docs and RHEL 7+ prefer ip
cards.notes: Know both for this course.

cards.front: ip address add IP/MASK dev IFACE
cards.meaning: Add a static IPv4 address to an interface (runtime)
cards.notes: Gone on reboot unless also written to distro config files.

cards.meaning: CIDR for netmask 255.255.255.0

cards.front: Two ip address add on same NIC
cards.meaning: A NIC can have more than one address active
cards.notes: Example output shows two inet lines on the same interface.

cards.meaning: Show addresses on that interface (addr = address)
cards.notes: Verify after add.

cards.meaning: Runtime only — vanish on reboot unless distro config is written
cards.notes: ifconfig/ip = now; ifcfg-* or /etc/network/interfaces = after reboot.

cards.front: ip route add HOST via GW dev IFACE
cards.meaning: Add a host route (single destination, typically /32)
cards.example: ip route add 192.0.2.1 via 10.0.0.2 dev eth0
cards.notes: via = next hop (gateway). dev = which NIC to send on.

cards.front: ip route add NET/MASK via GW dev IFACE
cards.meaning: Add a network route
cards.example: ip route add 192.0.2.0/24 via 10.0.0.3 dev eth0

cards.meaning: Next hop / gateway
Print the routing table
cards.notes: Look for default via.

cards.meaning: Default gateway — where unknown destinations go
cards.notes: No dest match → default via.

cards.meaning: Route preference; lower usually wins
Read /etc/sysconfig/network first, then ifcfg-* for up interfaces in numerically ascending order; last GATEWAY= wins
cards.notes: Prefer GATEWAY= in the per-interface ifcfg-* file.

cards.meaning: Deprecated on RHEL; put GATEWAY= in the per-interface ifcfg-* instead
cards.notes: Last GATEWAY= that is read still becomes the default route.

cards.meaning: Apply ifcfg changes on SysV / older RHEL
cards.notes: On systemd: systemctl restart network (or NetworkManager).

cards.meaning: Apply network config on systemd (or restart NetworkManager)
RHEL per-NIC persistent file: IP, mask, gateway, DHCP, on-boot
cards.notes: Memory hook: RHEL = ifcfg-eth0.

cards.meaning: RHEL global networking on/off, hostname (legacy gateway location)
cards.notes: GATEWAY here is deprecated; prefer ifcfg-*.

cards.meaning: DNS servers (nameserver lines) — both RHEL and Debian
cards.notes: Both families still use resolv.conf for DNS.

cards.meaning: Interface name in ifcfg file
Static IPv4 address in ifcfg
Subnet mask in ifcfg
Default gateway for that interface; preferred place for GATEWAY on RHEL
cards.notes: Last GATEWAY= read among up ifcfg files wins.

cards.meaning: Bring the interface up at boot
Ask DHCP for addressing
cards.notes: Static uses none/static plus IPADDR (omit dhcp).

cards.meaning: Static addressing — use with IPADDR (not dhcp)
Debian persistent interfaces: auto/iface, address, netmask, gateway
cards.notes: Memory hook: Debian = interfaces + hostname.

cards.meaning: Debian hostname (one line)
Debian stanza for a static IPv4 interface
cards.notes: Often paired with auto lo eth0.

cards.meaning: Name Service Switch — which sources to query and in what order
cards.notes: Phone book index for users, groups, hostnames, and more.

cards.meaning: Local files (/etc/passwd, /etc/hosts, …)
DNS server lookup source
NIS lookup source
LDAP lookup source
Database lookup source
Order = search order; first listed source is tried first
cards.notes: ping myhost may ignore /etc/hosts if dns comes first.

cards.meaning: Resolve hostnames via DNS, then NIS, then /etc/hosts
cards.notes: Why /etc/hosts can be skipped when dns is first.
